title: Which encoder should acre use for MP4 export instead of piping to ffmpeg?
body:
`acre render --out x.mp4` streams raw frames into an `ffmpeg` process that it finds on `PATH`. Jack wants export eventually not to depend on piping to an outside program. Piping is the stopgap until this is decided. The encoder lives in `acre-cli` whichever option wins, so the `acre` library stays free of it.

## Options

| option | how | cost |
|---|---|---|
| A. FFmpeg bindings (`ffmpeg-next`) | link the system's libavcodec and libavformat in-process, and encode with x264 where FFmpeg has it | needs FFmpeg dev headers and clang at build time, and ties acre to the system FFmpeg version; support for FFmpeg 9.0 is unchecked; best quality per byte |
| B. OpenH264 plus a Rust muxer (`openh264`, with `muxide` or `mp4`) | the crate compiles Cisco's OpenH264 from source, and a pure-Rust crate writes the MP4 container | needs only a C compiler; a weaker encoder than x264, which matters little for flat diagrams; Cisco's patent licence covers only their prebuilt binary, which matters for redistribution |
| C. Our own H.264 encoder | write it in acre | a full encoder is a large project; one that writes only keyframes makes very large files |
| D. AV1 with `rav1e` | a pure-Rust AV1 encoder in an MP4 | not H.264, so older players and some slide software cannot play it; slow to encode |

Leaning B: it is the one self-contained option, and its quality gap barely shows on flat graphics. A wins if the smallest files matter, or if formats beyond MP4 are wanted later.
